ruivo-acobreado: Copper red, a level 7 medium copper with a warm red undertone, like a polished new penny. Rich and saturated yet natural: deeper red-copper at the roots and underneath, glowing brighter amber-copper through the mid-lengths and ends where the light hits. Multi-tonal strands with subtle golden and red variations, even coverage from roots to ends with no darker regrowth, and the glossy, healthy shine of a realistic professional copper dye.
marsala: Marsala, a level 5 deep wine-brown with a muted red-violet tone, like dry red wine blended with earthy brown. Sophisticated and understated rather than bright: brownish burgundy in the shadows and at the roots, with soft garnet-wine reflections appearing on the surface in the light. Even from roots to ends with gentle strand-to-strand variation, never pink, neon purple or orange. Smooth satin shine of a realistic professional marsala dye.
vinho: Burgundy wine red, a level 4 deep red-violet with a rich, saturated purple-red tone like red wine in a glass. Dark plum-burgundy in the shadows and at the roots, vivid wine red with a cool violet glint wherever light touches the surface. Full, even coverage from roots to ends with natural multi-tonal variation between strands, intense but believable, never dull brown and never neon. Glossy, jewel-like shine of a realistic professional burgundy dye.
ruivo-natural: Natural redhead copper, a level 7-8 warm ginger-copper exactly like naturally red hair: an orange-copper base with golden strawberry strands and slightly deeper auburn-copper strands mixed throughout. Soft, believable saturation, never artificial or neon. Slightly richer at the roots and gently sun-lightened toward the ends, with fine natural variation from strand to strand and a soft healthy shine, so it reads as natural red hair rather than an obvious dye job.
cobre-intenso: Intense vivid copper, a level 7 highly saturated pure copper-orange with a metallic new-penny glow. Bold and fiery: glowing orange-copper on the surface, richer deep copper underneath, and bright amber highlights where the light hits. Strong uniform color from roots to ends with no darker regrowth and no brown cast, plus subtle multi-tonal variation between strands. High-gloss, luminous shine of a fresh professional copper color.
auburn: Auburn, a level 5 light-medium chestnut brown with a warm red-copper reflect, the brown base clearly infused with reddish copper. Mostly brown in the shadows and at the roots, revealing warm red and copper glints across the surface and the ends in the light. Natural, sophisticated and multi-tonal, with subtle variation between strands, never bright orange and never purple. Rich, glossy, healthy shine of a realistic professional auburn color.
vermelho-intenso: Intense true red, a level 6 vivid scarlet-crimson with a pure, highly saturated red tone, neither orange nor purple. Bold and striking: deep crimson in the shadows and underneath, bright glowing scarlet on the surface where the light hits. Full, even color from roots to ends with no regrowth, with subtle tonal variation between strands so it still looks like real dyed hair. High-gloss, luminous shine of a fresh professional red dye.
acaju: Acaju red mahogany, a level 5-6 reddish brown with a vivid red-mahogany reflect and a slight violet undertone. Clearly red rather than brown: warm cherry-wood red over a light brown base, deeper mahogany in the shadows and brighter garnet red on the surface in the light. Even from roots to ends with natural strand-to-strand variation, never orange and never neon purple. Rich, glossy shine of a realistic professional mahogany dye.
ruivo-cereja: Cherry red, a level 5-6 vivid cherry red with a cool pink-violet undertone, like a ripe glossy cherry. Saturated and juicy: deep black-cherry red in the shadows and underneath, brighter raspberry-cherry red on the surface where the light hits. Even coverage from roots to ends, never orange or coppery, with fine tonal variation between strands. Very glossy, almost lacquered shine of a realistic professional red dye.
mogno: Mahogany brown, a level 4 deep brown with a subtle red-violet mahogany reflect, like polished mahogany wood. Predominantly dark brown, with the reddish tone showing as a soft wine-red glow in light and sun rather than as obvious red. Darker and more neutral in the shadows and at the roots, warmer reddish brown on the surface. Natural multi-tonal strands, discreet and elegant, with the deep glossy shine of a realistic professional mahogany color.
loiro-morango: Strawberry blonde, a light level 8-9 golden blonde with a soft copper-rose tint, a delicate blend of pale gold and peachy strawberry red. Warm and luminous but subtle: rosy copper glints within golden blonde strands, slightly deeper apricot-copper near the roots and lighter sunlit strawberry gold on the ends. Multi-tonal and natural, never orange and never pastel pink. Soft, healthy shine of a realistic strawberry blonde salon result.
ginger: Ginger, a bright level 8 golden copper with a vivid orange-gold tone, warm and sunny like fresh ginger and marmalade. Lively saturated orange-copper with plenty of golden light in it: slightly deeper copper at the roots and underneath, luminous golden-ginger highlights on the surface and ends. Natural multi-tonal strands, never red-violet and never brown. Healthy glossy shine of a realistic professional ginger color.
cobre-claro: Light soft copper, a level 8-9 pale copper blonde with a gentle apricot-peach tone. Airy, light and warm rather than intense: soft peach-copper blended with light golden strands, a touch deeper copper close to the roots and lighter, almost peachy blonde on the ends. Delicate, even coverage with natural variation between strands, never deep orange and never red. Luminous satin shine of a realistic professional light copper color.
ruivo-canela: Cinnamon copper brown, a level 6 warm light brown with a golden-copper reflect, like ground cinnamon. A soft blend of brown and copper: warm brown in the depth and at the roots, spicy copper-gold glints across the surface and slightly brighter cinnamon tones on the ends. Natural, multi-tonal and understated, less red than auburn and less orange than pure copper. Rich, healthy shine of a realistic professional color.
ruivo-escuro: Dark copper, a level 5-6 deep saturated copper-red with a rich burnt-orange intensity. Darker than classic copper yet still clearly red-copper rather than brown: dark rusty copper in the shadows and at the roots, glowing deep amber-copper on the surface in the light. Even from roots to ends with natural tonal variation between strands and no dull brown cast. Lush, glossy shine of a realistic professional dark copper dye.
cherry-cola: Cherry cola, a level 3 very dark brown-black base with a deep cherry-red and violet reflect, like cola with a cherry glow. Looks almost black-brown in the shadows and at the roots, while surfaces catching the light reveal a rich dark cherry-burgundy shimmer. Subtle, sultry and multi-tonal, with natural variation between strands, never bright red. Deep, high-gloss shine of a realistic professional dark red color.
ruivo-fogo: Fire red, a level 7 vivid red-orange with a hot copper-red tone, halfway between bright red and copper, like flames. Saturated and radiant: deep red-copper underneath, glowing orange-red and fiery scarlet on the surface where the light hits. Even coverage from roots to ends with no regrowth, never pink or purple, with natural flickering variation between strands. High, luminous shine of a realistic professional red-copper dye.
cobre-rose: Rose copper, a level 8 light copper with a soft pink-rosé tone, a romantic blend of peachy copper and dusty rose gold. Warm yet rosy: copper-pink strands mixed with lighter rosé-gold strands, a touch deeper rosy copper near the roots and softer, lighter rose-peach on the ends. Delicate saturation that still reads as natural copper, never bubblegum pink and never orange. Silky, luminous shine of a realistic professional toned result.
red-velvet: Red velvet, a level 4-5 deep crimson red with a rich, slightly brownish velvety tone, like red velvet cake. Dark ruby-crimson in the shadows and at the roots, with luminous blood-red highlights on the surface in the light. Intense and saturated but darker and more sophisticated than bright red, never orange and never purple. Even coverage with natural strand-to-strand variation and a velvety, glossy shine of a realistic professional red dye.
ruivo-alaranjado: Bright orange red, a level 8 vivid tangerine orange, the most orange of the copper shades: pure saturated orange over a slightly warm red base. Bold and cheerful: deeper orange underneath and glowing tangerine-apricot on the surface and ends. Strong, even color from roots to ends with no darker regrowth, never pink and never brown, with subtle tonal variation between strands. Glossy, radiant shine of a realistic professional orange-copper dye.
pumpkin-spice: Pumpkin spice, a level 6-7 burnt orange copper with warm brown-spice depth, like pumpkin and nutmeg. Rich and earthy rather than neon: deeper brownish copper at the roots and underneath, glowing pumpkin orange and golden copper through the mid-lengths and ends. Multi-tonal, with soft cinnamon-brown lowlights woven between orange strands. Warm, autumnal and natural, with the soft glossy shine of a realistic professional copper color.
ruivo-veneziano: Venetian Titian red, a level 7 golden red-copper with soft rosy-red reflections, like the red-gold hair in Renaissance paintings. Warm and refined: a golden copper base enriched with strands of soft auburn red and strawberry gold, slightly deeper at the roots and brighter red-gold on the ends. Softer and more golden than bright red, yet redder than ginger. Natural multi-tonal variation and a luminous, silky shine of a realistic professional color.
bronde-acobreado: Copper bronde, a multi-tonal blend of level 6 light brown, level 8 golden blonde and soft copper, creating a warm sun-kissed bronze effect. Fine strands of golden blonde and light copper intertwine with light brown throughout, slightly deeper brown-copper at the roots melting seamlessly into brighter copper-gold through the mid-lengths and ends. Softly dimensional, never stripy and never orange. Natural, glossy shine of a realistic professional blended color.
ruivo-terracota: Terracotta, a level 6 earthy brick red-orange with a muted, dusty clay tone, like fired terracotta pottery. Warm, natural and softly desaturated: rosy brick-copper on the surface, deeper rust-brown in the shadows and at the roots, never neon orange and never bright red. Even coverage with natural multi-tonal variation between strands, a hint of rosy brown, and a soft satin shine for a realistic, modern earthy red result.
cowboy-copper: Cowboy copper, a level 6-7 muted brown-copper inspired by worn leather cowboy boots: rich copper blended with warm chestnut brown and a hint of caramel, softer and browner than bright ginger. Slightly deeper brown-copper at the roots melting seamlessly into warmer, brighter leathery copper through the mid-lengths and ends, with fine multi-tonal strands of copper, amber and brown for dimension. Never neon orange and never flat brown. Rich, glossy, realistic professional copper result.
